Step 1.1 overloads a_i,b_j as vectors and scalars. The intended matrix-unit proof is sound, but its notation is ill-typed; renamed eigenvectors u_i,v_j and wrote Au_i=a_i u_i, Bv_j=b_j v_j. The matrix units are linear under the linear-first convention, are Hilbert-Schmidt orthonormal, and have positive eigenvalues b_j/a_i. The logarithm formula and cyclic trace identity then give D(A||B) without assuming A and B commute. Statement unchanged; nonfatal notation repair.

The state and entropy computations are correct, but the displayed F6 only states the reciprocal-log identity and leaves the final strict sign unexplained. Added strict monotonicity and ln(1)=0 from the already declared thm-natural-logarithm-laws, and used 2>1 to obtain ln(2)>0. Both marginals are I_2/2 and the joint spectrum is 1,0,0,0, so S(A|B)=-ln(2)<0. Nonfatal missing explanation; Example unchanged.

The unqualified finiteness assertion fails for p_0=1, rho_0=diag(1,0), p_1=0, rho_1=diag(0,1): bar rho=rho_0 and D(rho_1||bar rho)=+infinity by support failure. The displayed unrestricted sum in step 3.1 can then contain undefined 0 times infinity. Restricted finiteness and the divergence sum explicitly to p_x>0, and justified trace linearity using the common support logarithm extended by zero. The support argument and channel data processing now sum to the unchanged Holevo bound for all allowed ensembles. Fatal logic defect in the written finiteness/sum claim, rather than a false theorem.
